newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says finalises j/v deal with ABB.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says finalises j/v deal with ABB.

text.p: Swedish vehicle company AB Volvo said on Monday its car unit had signed the final agreement with Swedish-Swiss engineering company ABB over a joint venture in assembly line engineering and press automation.
Swedish vehicle maker Volvo and ABB announced plans for the joint venture in December and signed the final agreement on Monday.
"The company will manufacture and market automation equipment for automotive body assembly shops and press lines," Volvo said in a statement.
Volvo Car holds 49 percent and ABB holds 51 percent of the joint venture company, ABB Olofstrom Automation.
The board of directors consists of five members with the chairman appointed by ABB.

The new company includes the former Volvo Cars' business for assembly line engineering, press automation and lightweight welding guns in Olofstrom, Sweden, as well as Olofstrom Automation in Toronto, Canada, in Detroit in the U.S., and Sao Paolo in Brazil.
ABB Olofstrom Automation employs 260 people in Sweden and 250 in North America.
The new company is part of ABB Flexible Automation, a business area within ABB's Industrial and Building Systems segment.
